# Security Checklist: Mission Control Product-Line Seed and Flag Activation

**Purpose**: Validate that SPEC-009B requirements and plan artifacts fully define redacted evidence, credential-safe logging, non-destructive cleanup boundaries, and operator-confirmed cleanup verification.
**Created**: 2026-05-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are cleanup documentation and evidence requirements complete enough to exclude raw secrets, token values, Authorization headers, API keys, passwords, and credential-like substrings while still allowing cleanup-safe identifiers? [Completeness, Spec §FR-028, Contract §Security Requirements]
- [ ] CHK002 Are seed, preflight, checklist, and log evidence requirements complete enough to prevent GitHub and OpenClaw credentials from appearing in JSON output, Markdown evidence, errors, or operator-facing summaries? [Completeness, Spec §FR-028, Contract §Seed Evidence]
- [ ] CHK003 Are non-Mission-Control cleanup boundaries complete enough to prohibit automatic deletion, unlinking, or mutation of live project, ticket, GitHub sync, cron, OpenClaw/gateway, or FocusEngine residue? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-027, Data Model §Cleanup Residue]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec require explicit operator confirmation before live cleanup actions and post-cleanup verification before deployment proceeds? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK005 Are backup/export-first requirements defined for every operator cleanup target named by the feature, including FocusEngine project state, tickets, GitHub sync configuration, OpenClaw/gateway agents, and issue-sync cron? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, Spec §FR-013, Spec §SC-010]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is the distinction between cleanup-safe identifiers and forbidden credential values clear enough for evidence authors to know what can be emitted? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028, Contract §Security Requirements]
- [ ] CHK007 Is `mutation_status: "not_mutated"` unambiguously tied to blocked preflight and contract readiness failures before any seed mutation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Contract §Modes, Contract §Seed Evidence Validation Rules]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the phrase "no automatic cleanup" specific enough to cover deletion, unlinking, mutation, task status rewrites, GitHub sync changes, cron changes, and OpenClaw/gateway changes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-027, Plan §Implementation Approach]
- [ ] CHK009 Are credential-redaction requirements clear that matched secret substrings must not be emitted even when the surrounding error or evidence object is useful to operators? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028, Spec §Assumptions, Contract §Security Requirements]
- [ ] CHK010 Are blocked cleanup readiness, seed implementation failure, and successful deployment evidence distinct enough to avoid treating a blocked security preflight as a successful seed? [Clarity, Spec §Spec Evidence And Archive Policy, Contract §Evidence Sections]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Do the spec, plan, data model, and CLI contract consistently require residue preflight to complete before seed mutation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Plan §Summary, Data Model §State Transitions, Contract §Modes]
- [ ] CHK012 Do the security requirements align with the plan's defensive-boundary statement that file reads, DB open, preflight scans, workflow-contract loading, and external evidence parsing return structured, redacted results? [Consistency, Plan §Constitution Check, Constitution §XIII]
- [ ] CHK013 Do cleanup requirements consistently preserve non-Mission-Control state while delegating live cleanup to an operator-owned backup/export-first runbook? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-013, Plan §Implementation Approach]
- [ ] CHK014 Do non-dispatch and non-deletion requirements align so security evidence cannot be satisfied by creating synthetic issue work, claiming tasks, or deleting existing residue? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023, Spec §FR-024, Spec §SC-009]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Can redaction success be objectively measured by evidence fields proving `raw_secret_values_emitted: false` and by allowed identifier classes? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-028, Contract §Seed Evidence]
- [ ] CHK016 Can non-destructive blocked preflight be objectively measured by `mutation_status: "not_mutated"` plus unchanged before/after row and file snapshots for non-Mission-Control residue? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-005, Contract §Seed Evidence Validation Rules]
- [ ] CHK017 Can operator cleanup readiness be objectively measured through backup/export proof, explicit confirmation, and verification that only `racecraft-lab/mission-control` issue sync remains before deployment? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK018 Can non-dispatch security boundaries be objectively measured with zero synthetic GitHub issues, claims, dispatches, runner rows, sandbox rows, auto-merge paths, and post-merge reconciliation side effects? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-009, Contract §Seed Evidence]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are exception scenarios covered for credential-bearing GitHub/OpenClaw errors so they produce useful redacted payloads rather than raw stderr, headers, tokens, or config bodies? [Coverage, Spec §FR-028, Contract §Exit Codes]
- [ ] CHK020 Are cleanup-doc scenarios covered for both blocked preflight evidence before cleanup and post-cleanup evidence after the operator has removed residue? [Coverage, Spec §SC-005, Spec §SC-010, Contract §Evidence Sections]
- [ ] CHK021 Are edge cases covered where external operator evidence contains credential-like values, requiring redaction while retaining host aliases, config paths, counts, timestamps, booleans, and hashes? [Coverage, Spec §FR-027, Spec §FR-028, Data Model §Cleanup Residue]
- [ ] CHK022 Are edge cases covered where unrelated live project or ticket data exists and must remain preserved even though it blocks SPEC-009B deployment readiness? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-011, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK023 Are security dependencies on the existing redaction/auditability conventions documented clearly enough to keep seed evidence durable without leaking credentials? [Dependency, Constitution §X, Constitution §XIII, Spec §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK024 Are assumptions about operator-owned FocusEngine cleanup explicit enough to prevent SPEC-009B from adding a FocusEngine domain entity, automatic cleanup command, or credential-bearing cleanup export? [Dependency, Spec §FR-027, Spec §Assumptions]

## Remediation Verification

- [ ] CHK025 Does the remediated spec explicitly require backup/export-first cleanup, operator confirmation before destructive cleanup commands, and post-cleanup verification before deployment proceeds? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK026 Does the remediated plan carry the same explicit-confirmation and verification boundary for pre-deploy cleanup documentation? [Consistency, Plan §Technical Context, Plan §Implementation Approach, Plan §Validation Plan]
- [ ] CHK027 Are GitHub/OpenClaw credentials and matched secret substrings now explicitly excluded from cleanup documents, seed evidence, preflight evidence, checklist evidence, logs, and errors? [Completeness, Spec §FR-028, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 Can the security checklist be evaluated without relying on hidden terminal context because each remediated item cites the spec, plan, contract, data model, or constitution source? [Traceability, Spec §FR-026]
